First discovered over a decade ago in 2007 @Lorimer07, it was not until 2017 that an FRB was precisely localized and traced back to its host galaxy at $z = 0.19$, providing the first direct evidence of their cosmological origins #cite(<Chatterjee-17>)#cite(<Marcote-17>)#cite(<Tendulkar-17>). While this first localization was facilitated by targeted observations made possible by the repeating nature of the source, an increasing number of FRBs are now being localized upon detection by fast transient searches using radio interferometers #cite(<Bannister-19>)#cite(<Ravi-19>). Over the last decade, the commissioning of sensitive and wide-field fast transient detection instrumentation has led to an enormous increase in the detected FRB population #cite(<CHIME-18>)#cite(<Macquart-10>). It is now established that some fraction (currently $tilde$4\% observed; #cite(<Petroff-22>, form: "prose")) of the FRB population produce repeat bursts from the same cosmic source #cite(<Spitler-16>)@chime-repeater while the majority of discovered FRBs have not been observed to repeat to date @CHIME-catalog. Despite over 600 published FRBs to date #cite(<Petroff-22>), their origins and the nature of their repetition remains uncertain.
